title_en: Provisions of the State Council on Working Hours of Employees

articles.content_en: Article 1 These Provisions are formulated in accordance with the relevant provisions of the Constitution for the purposes of rationally arranging the working and rest hours of employees, safeguarding their right to rest, mobilizing their enthusiasm, and promoting the development of socialist modernization.

Article 2 These Provisions shall apply to employees of state organs, social organizations, enterprises, public institutions, and other organizations within the territory of the People's Republic of China.
Article 3 Employees shall work 8 hours per day and 40 hours per week.

Article 4 Where employees engaged in labor under special conditions or in special circumstances need to have their working hours appropriately shortened, the matter shall be handled in accordance with the relevant provisions of the State.

Article 5 Where the standard working hour system of 8 hours per day and 40 hours per week cannot be implemented due to the nature of work or production characteristics, other working and rest methods may be adopted in accordance with the relevant provisions of the State.

Article 6 No unit or individual shall extend employees' working hours without authorization. Where extension of working hours is truly necessary due to special circumstances or urgent tasks, the matter shall be handled in accordance with the relevant provisions of the State.

Article 7 State organs and public institutions shall implement uniform working hours, with Saturday and Sunday as the weekly rest days.
Enterprises and public institutions that are unable to implement the uniform working hours as prescribed in the preceding paragraph may, in light of actual circumstances, flexibly arrange the weekly rest days.

Article 8 These Provisions shall be interpreted by the Ministry of Labor and the Ministry of Personnel; the implementation measures shall be formulated by the Ministry of Labor and the Ministry of Personnel.

Article 9 These Provisions shall come into force as of May 1, 1995. Enterprises and public institutions that encounter difficulties in implementation as of May 1, 1995 may appropriately postpone the implementation; however, public institutions shall implement them no later than January 1, 1996, and enterprises shall implement them no later than May 1, 1997.
